query: Consider the following context: Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications. In that context, which method can be used for tuning the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Varying the non‐equiatomic composition by adjusting the relative elemental ratios in high‐entropy alloys systematically tunes the magnetic interactions, thereby modulating the magnetic phase transition and enhancing the magnetocaloric effect.
generation.material_initial_state: Non‐equiatomic high‐entropy alloys with a baseline composition exhibiting a characteristic magnetic phase transition.
generation.intervention: Systematic adjustment of the elemental ratios (i.e., non‐equiatomic tuning) while maintaining the overall alloy framework.
generation.conditions: Ambient or application-relevant temperatures and pressures in low-dimensional sample geometries, with constant processing and annealing conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Local atomic disorder and variable exchange interaction networks arising from the altered elemental ratios.
generation.mechanism: Changing the relative concentrations of constituent elements alters local magnetic exchange interactions and modifies the magnetic ordering temperature (TC). This, in turn, shifts the phase transition that drives the magnetocaloric effect, potentially allowing optimization of entropy change for improved cooling performance.
generation.predicted_outcome: A shift in the magnetic phase transition temperature and an enhancement (or tuning) of the magnetocaloric effect, such that samples with optimized compositions show measurable differences (e.g., in TC and ΔS) compared to the baseline alloy.
generation.baseline: A non‐equiatomic HEA with fixed elemental ratios exhibiting baseline magnetic and magnetocaloric properties.
generation.boundary: The results are expected to hold for non‐equiatomic HEAs and may not directly extend to equiatomic alloys or systems where other external factors (e.g., extreme processing conditions) overshadow compositional tuning effects.
generation.uncertainty: The exact proportional changes needed in elemental composition to achieve a quantitatively optimal magnetocaloric enhancement remain undetermined and likely depend on the specific elements involved.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of non‐equiatomic HEA samples with systematically varied elemental ratios while keeping processing, annealing, and dimensions constant. Use magnetometric and calorimetric techniques to track variations in magnetic transition temperatures and the magnitude of the magnetocaloric effect.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If variations in elemental ratios do not result in any significant shifts in the magnetic transition temperature or measurable changes in the magnetocaloric effect compared to the baseline composition, the hypothesis will be falsified.
